subject: Residency statement and temporary cross-region egress addendum request
messages:
From: Lina Patel <lina.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Residency question — short-term cross-region processing for migration

Hi Karthik,

Quick background: Acme is migrating our EU analytics cluster and expect a 48–96 hour window where a subset of EU production requests will be routed to US-based tooling for backfill and dedupe. Our privacy/security team needs a written statement that (a) primary processing remains EU, (b) temporary cross-region processing will be limited to specific job IDs and duration, and (c) all data handled during that window will be logged, encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys, and retained only as necessary.

Please also attach your latest subprocessor roster and any DPA-addendum language you recommend for this temporary egress. We need this for our internal approvers and to attach to our change request.

Thanks,
Lina
Lina Patel
Senior Procurement Manager — Acme Health
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Lina Patel <lina.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 18:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Residency question — short-term cross-region processing for migration

Hi Lina — thanks for the note and context. Below is a concise residency statement and the operational commitments we can make for a short-term egress window. I've attached a short playbook and our current subprocessor roster for your legal and security teams.

Residency statement (summary):
- Primary inference and storage for Acme Health customer data will remain within the EU region(s) specified in your contract except for explicitly authorized temporary tasks.
- Temporary cross-region processing is permissible for a limited, pre-authorized maintenance window (max 96 hours) tied to named job IDs and surge buckets.
- During the window, data transferred out of the EU will be: encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3), encrypted at rest with customer-provided KMS keys where requested, and subject to full audit logging.
- Any transient replicas/exports will be deleted within 7 days of job completion unless you request a different retention.

Operational controls we will enable for the window:
- Job-level allowlist: only job IDs submitted by Acme-runbook will be permitted to cross regions.
- KMS enforcement: we will attach your KMS key to transient storage where feasible.
- Audit collection: request/response logs for impacted requests, per-token telemetry, and routing decisions will be exported to a restricted log bucket in EU and a temporary, access-controlled US audit bucket with read access only to named Redwood ops staff.
- Network restrictions: egress will be limited to specific IP ranges and cloud accounts; we will provide those ranges 48 hours before the window.

Attachments included: temp-egress-playbook.pdf (ops runbook), subprocessor-roster.csv (latest export), dpa-addendum-draft.docx (suggested language).

Next steps: If that looks good, Markus (legal) can review the addendum redline and we can produce a DocuSign link for a one-off amendment. Lauren — can you confirm operational readiness/timeline?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Lina Patel <lina.patel@acmehealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:47:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Residency question — short-term cross-region processing for migration

Thanks Karthik — reading through the draft addendum I made two small clarifications for Acme's legal team: (1) explicitly state that the temporary egress is subject to documented authorizations and a maximum cumulative duration per quarter (we recommend 96 hours but will also accept a per-quarter cap), and (2) require that Redwood provide evidence of deletion of transient replicas (screenshot + audit id) within the agreed SLA.

I added inline comments to dpa-addendum-draft.docx and flagged a short clause for emergency exceptions (requires exec sign-off).

This should be light-touch for procurement but gives Acme the evidence they need for auditors.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Lina Patel <lina.patel@acmehealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 13:22:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Residency question — short-term cross-region processing for migration

Hi Lina — ops confirmation below. We can support the window with these operational notes:
- Timeline: we need 48 hours notice for IP allowlist and KMS handshake; provisioning typically completes within 24 hours of notice.
- Scoped routing: we will implement a temporary policy keyed by job IDs and routing tags; any traffic without the tag will be blocked from crossing region.
- Logs & proof: audit IDs for deletion + export of log manifests will be provided to Acme SRE team.
- Monitoring: we will add a dashboard for the window showing routing counts, latency, and bytes egressed.
- Rollback: if any data or access anomalies occur we will suspend the window and present remediation steps within 2 hours.

I'll coordinate the runbook execution and will attach the IP ranges and a short checklist 48 hours before the planned window.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Principal Engineer, Operations — Redwood Inference

Lina
